summary: The counters and their side scenes establish what each market sells. Some transactions promise stock, payment or correspondence that the available choices and current game state do not support.

issues.problem: The opening always says there is a rare item on the curio cloth. On a visit whose scheduled curio the player already owns, all three curio choices disappear.
issues.fix: Give the cloth a sold-out or display-only line for those visits, or rotate to an unowned item when one remains.

issues.problem: When the player makes up the price difference, Grimsby says he will pay them back. There is no repayment in the branch or later hook. The round-two author notes say the promise was removed, but it is present in the frozen source.
issues.fix: Have him thank the player for a gift, or arrange for him to repay the difference later.

issues.problem: A player with zero crowns can accept the bet and lose. The outcome says they paid full price and received the hat even though they paid nothing.
issues.fix: Gate the wager on being able to pay the quoted price, or charge the price as a stake and return it on a win.

issues.problem: Copying the chart is Hollow, but the seller watches, smiles, and says everyone copies it. The branch gives no reason that copying a chart he openly shares should carry a moral cost.
issues.fix: Show the player violating a clear condition of seeing the chart, or give copying a cost the shop encounter actually establishes.

issues.problem: The Guile lesson claims the tutor charges extra, but its cost is the same as every other lesson in the menu.
issues.fix: Remove the surcharge claim or put the intended fee in the option price.

issues.problem: Kael's paid reply is described as coming from the North. His break schedule specifically keeps him by the lake and observatory at the academy because he cannot go home.
issues.fix: Have the letter find him at the academy. Keep the frost as something he does to the envelope.
